beats.headline: Apple jumps on record earnings and $100B buyback
beats.explanation: Apple gained 3.24% to close at $280.14 on 1.9 times its average volume following record quarterly results, upbeat guidance, and a $100 billion share buyback announcement. The move was primarily company-specific, with connected peers like customer Alphabet up just 0.23% and supplier TSMC up 0.41%, even as competitor Intel advanced 5.44%.

beats.headline: Apple falls as WWDC and Siri AI disappoint
beats.explanation: Apple dropped 3.65% to $290.55 after unveiling its WWDC updates, with investors questioning device upgrade cycles and noting the AI announcements fell short of high expectations. Competitors Intel and Microsoft also dropped 2.13% and 2.02% respectively, while supplier Qualcomm dropped 5.67%, reflecting broader sector softness alongside Apple's event reaction.

beats.headline: Apple sinks 6.12% after mid-cycle product price hikes
beats.explanation: Shares fell 6.12% to $275.15 on 2.6 times average volume after Apple raised prices across Macs, iPads, and accessories to offset surging AI-driven memory chip costs. The steep drop was distinct from peers like supplier Qualcomm, which gained 3.79%, and competitor Intel, which rose 0.93%, as the market reacted to margin pressures and demand concerns.

beats.headline: Apple rebounds 3.14% on technical bounce
beats.explanation: Apple rebounded 3.14% to $283.78 on massive volume of 6.3 times normal, regaining ground from technical support near the $275 level following the prior session's price-hike sell-off. The rebound occurred despite negative headline news of its Vision Pro hardware lead defecting to OpenAI, and diverged from suppliers Cirrus Logic and Qualcomm, which slid 4.86% and 7.57% respectively.

beats.headline: Apple climbs 4.84% on foldable iPhone targets
beats.explanation: Shares rose 4.84% to $308.63 following reports that Apple expanded production plans for its upcoming foldable iPhone to roughly 10 million units and prepared an aggressive five-model lineup. The advance was company-specific, as suppliers Cirrus Logic, Qualcomm, and TSMC fell between 0.12% and 3.12%, while competitor Intel dropped 5.25%.

beats.headline: Apple hits record high on China AI regulatory approval
beats.explanation: Apple surged 4.01% to a new all-time high of $327.50 after Chinese regulators approved Apple Intelligence in the country via integration with Alibaba's Qwen model. While competitor Microsoft and customer Alphabet also posted gains of 2.78% and 3.17%, Apple outperformed its suppliers TSMC and Qualcomm, which were slightly negative.

beats.headline: Apple gains 3.53% on capital-light AI strategy
beats.explanation: Apple rose 3.53% to $333.02 as market sentiment favored its anti-capex AI approach heading into earnings, treating the stock as a hedge against heavy infrastructure spending by tech peers. The gain was distinct to Apple, with competitor Intel dropping 7.89% and suppliers TSMC and Qualcomm retreating 2.93% and 2.42%.

beats.headline: Apple drops 7.35% on weak guidance from chip shortages
beats.explanation: Apple slid 7.35% to $308.91 on 3.2 times average volume after its fiscal third-quarter report included weaker-than-expected sales guidance caused by AI-driven component shortages. The plunge was sharply company-specific, occurring while customer Alphabet and competitor Microsoft rose 6.73% and 3.02% respectively on strong cloud results.

beats.headline: Apple rises 3.56% following iPhone Duo launch
beats.explanation: Apple shares climbed 3.56% to $326.57 as analysts projected strong demand for the newly announced $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo against rival Samsung. The move was accompanied by supplier Cirrus Logic jumping 5.20%, while competitor Intel fell 5.57% and supplier TSMC shed 1.68%.

arc: Between May and September 2026, Apple traded within an aggressive multi-month tug-of-war between strong hardware demand initiatives and the severe supply-chain friction of the broader AI cycle. The company opened the period strong with record earnings and a $100 billion buyback, but quickly faced headwinds as AI-driven component and memory shortages forced rare mid-cycle hardware price hikes on Macs and iPads, culminating in a 7.35% post-earnings plunge on July 31 due to component-constrained guidance. Nevertheless, Apple steadily built resilience by maintaining a low-capex AI model, securing regulatory clearance for Apple Intelligence in China, and unveiling the flagship foldable iPhone Duo, enabling the stock to recover back toward the $326 level.
